STEP 1 - Scene: A single slice of bread (looks like a sourdough or rustic white loaf with an open crumb and a toasted/browned crust edge) on a white square plate. Photographed from above, nearly top-down.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white plate is roughly square, about 24 cm across its width (comparable to a dinner plate). Plate area ≈ 24 × 24 × ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 490 cm²; I'll use ~480 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: One slice of bread. No visible oil, spread, or sauce.

STEP 4 - Area: The slice spans roughly 220 px by 260 px in a plate that measures about 460 px across, so the slice covers about 17% of the plate area (≈ 80 cm²).

STEP 5 - Volume: Slice is about 1.5 cm thick (typical sandwich slice, a bit thicker for rustic bread). 80 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 120 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Bread-like slice bulk density ~0.9 g/ml is too high for an airy open-crumb loaf; using the bread-loaf figure of ~0.3 g/ml for this porous crumb gives 120 × 0.3 ≈ 36 g. A typical slice of this size is about 30–40 g, consistent.

STEP 7 - Energy: White bread/rustic white bread ≈ 265 kcal per 100 g. 36 g × 2.65 ≈ 95 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: One slice of bread weighing ~36 g and ~95 kcal is plausible for what is visible. Nothing else is on the plate.

Total: about 36 g, about 95 kcal.
